title: Independence is named the center place of Zion
setting: Joseph Smith reached Independence, Jackson County, Missouri, on 14 July 1831. A June revelation had sent him and other elders there from Ohio. Oliver Cowdery and other missionaries were already in the area after preaching to American Indians. Joseph Smith later wrote that he pondered those people and asked when and where Zion would be built. He dictated this revelation on 20 July; the original is lost.
summary: The revelation tells the elders gathered in Missouri that this land is appointed for the gathering of the Saints. It calls it the land of promise and the place for the city of Zion. Independence is the center place, and a temple lot lies west of the courthouse. The Saints are to buy land there and westward to the line “between Jew and Gentile,” as far as they can. Sidney Gilbert is to act as agent, buy land, and open a store. Edward Partridge is to divide inheritances to the Saints. William W. Phelps is to be printer, with Oliver Cowdery helping to copy and correct. These men are to settle in Zion, and the bishop and agent are to prepare for arriving families.

contextNote.title: A place on the map at last
contextNote.text: For months the city of Zion had no known location. An 1830 revelation had placed it only on the borders by the Lamanites (D&C 28:9). Verse 3 answers with a town and a lot: Independence, west of the courthouse. Verse 4 turns that answer into a task, telling the Saints to buy the land. Verses 6–8 then assign people to handle money, land, and goods. In this passage, “center place” names a real site to be purchased and settled.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 51–57 treats the work in Zion as stewardship. In verses 6–13, what task does each named man receive, and how does each serve the gathering?
reviewNote: Read all 16 verses. Official heading gives Zion, Jackson County, Missouri, 20 July 1831, and Joseph Smith’s pondering about the Lamanites and Zion. JSP historical introduction gave the 14 July arrival, companions, earlier missionaries, and lost original. The 1830 phrase quoted in the context note is from D&C 28:9, cited by JSP. indian-lands added because the setting and v. 4 border line require it. Build review 2026-10-12: replaced the 1830 manuscript wording of 28:9 with the current wording.
